headline: A new rainstorm moves in Friday. What does it means for L.A. Halloween?
author: Alex Wigglesworth

paragraphs.text: As if Southern California hasn’t seen enough wild weather, a new storm is moving in just in time for Halloween.
Storms will start to arrive Friday, with stray showers in isolated areas and maximum temperatures 5 to 10 degrees below normal, according to the forecast from the National Weather Service.

The storm system likely will peak Saturday evening into Sunday morning, with a 70% chance of rain, the forecast states. Although forecasters still aren’t sure how much rain will fall, it’s most likely to total half an inch to an inch, said Ryan Kittell, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service in Oxnard.
The latest projections have the rain peaking between 9 p.m. Saturday and 9 a.m. Sunday, Kittell said.
“I think people should still plan for rain for Halloween activities, but right now it looks more on the lighter side than moderate side” earlier in the evening, he said.
The last recorded rainfall on Halloween in L.A. occurred in 2014, when a quarter of an inch of precipitation fell on downtown Los Angeles, according to weather service records.

Impacts of the storm are expected to be minimal, with the potential for increased traffic and minor roadway flooding, Kittell said. “Probably the biggest impact would be on Halloween activities,” he said.
